notes.summary: All-cone, all-Reeb finite-energy target criterion: finite explicit FS dual energy is equivalent to integrating every actual E1 potential and is necessary for genuine MA outputs. Image sufficiency remains unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: Using the explicitly accepted full P13.1 mathematical theorem, the reference MA is the trivial-valuation Dirac probability. Actual fixed-ray mixed-product expansion gives J(tu)≤2^n t²J(u). A decreasing convex-series argument proves the converse integrability criterion. The FS, CPSH and E1 dual suprema coincide, and decreasing target integrals are continuous for arbitrary nets. The finite-energy measure class is independent of Reeb field on K. Tangency proves necessity and optimality for every genuine output. No completeness or inverse existence is asserted.
notes.text:
Let k be any algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, (X,T;ξ) any normal good polarized affine cone, n=dim X≥1, p=n−1, and K=X0^T. All potentials below are the actual cone classes restricted to K. The mathematical supporting premise is the explicitly accepted FULL P13.1 proof at /workspace/research/deliverables/original-P13.1/P13.1-reviewed-argument.md, SHA256 de75b9ae55fbeb63c605505a328ed306c321a8e674331827cde51f5cfad76609. Its operational claims and canonical notes are not separate mathematical premises. It supplies actual-class convexity, genuine fixed-field decreasing energy and weighted mixed-MA continuity, positive mixed probabilities, integration by parts, Hodge index, intrinsic roots and normalized E1 transport, and canonical outer differentiation. It supplies no envelope attainment, actual completeness or inverse.

The actual probability is νξ(u1,…,up)=Vξ^(−1)ddc u1⋯ddc up ddc ρξ^+, and Eξ(u)=(nVξ)^(−1)Σ_(j=0)^p∫K u(ddc u)^j(ddc ρξ)^(p−j)ddc ρξ^+. Finite-energy expressions use genuine same-field decreasing limits. At a rational field η=sηe, using its effective supported gcd-one grading and actual degree-d Veronese cover, the accepted normal quotient has dimension p and Vη=s^(−n)d^(1−n)(Ld^p), ωη=Ld/(sd), ωη^p=sVη, Eη=E_Ld/(sd). Single-degree Hilbert coefficients are (Ld^p)/p!, cutoff coefficients Vη/n!, and the signed full-ring bridge is E=(n+1)S/n. These retain the radial unit mass, finite-map degree d and n factors 1/(sd).

The reference MA is δ_vtriv. Rationally its zero-weight product model has one central component, multiplicity one and mixed intersection Ld^p; its probability is the trivial-valuation Dirac mass. The accepted radial lift gives vtriv on K. Irrational references are bounded local uniform limits of rational references, so accepted genuine bounded current continuity gives the same mass. No unbounded potential moves its field. Normalize u(vtriv)=supK u=0; then u≤0 and J(u)=−E(u).

For a Radon probability μ on K define Lξ(μ)=sup_(w∈H(ξ))[Eξ(w)−∫K w dμ]. Each test is an explicit finite primary homogeneous FS maximum. Uniform FS approximation and energy continuity equate this supremum with CPSH. For a decreasing bounded-above usc net h_i↓h on compact Hausdorff K, ∫h_i dμ↓∫h dμ: Radon regularity expresses the integral as an infimum over continuous majorants; for g≥h, the increasing open sets {h_i<g+ε} cover K, so compactness and directedness give h_i≤g+ε eventually. Infimize over g and let ε decrease to zero. This includes extended integrals and nonmetrizable carriers.

If Lξ(μ)<∞ and u_i↓u is an actual CPSH defining net of u∈E1, then ∫u_i dμ≥E(u_i)−L. Both decreasing continuities imply ∫u dμ≥E(u)−L>−∞. Since u is bounded above, it is L1. Passing E(u_i)−∫u_i to the limit proves Lξ(μ)=sup_(u∈E1)[E(u)−∫u dμ]=Eξ^∨(μ). If the bounded-test supremum is infinite, the E1 supremum is also infinite.

For the converse, let b_l=−∫u dνξ(u repeated l times,ρ repeated p−l times) for normalized actual E1 u. Weighted mixed continuity makes these finite and nonnegative; b_0=0 by the reference Dirac, and J(u)=Σb_l/n. The actual segment u_t=tu+(1−t)ρ, 0≤t≤1, satisfies
J(u_t)=(1/n)Σ_(l=1)^p[tΣ_(j=l)^p binom(j,l)t^l(1−t)^(j−l)]b_l≤2^n t²J(u).
Indeed t^(l+1)≤t² and Σ_(j=l)^p binom(j,l)=binom(n,l+1)≤2^n. This passes from CPSH to E1 by genuine fixed-field decreasing continuity; no linear cross-ray axioms are inferred from roots.

Suppose every actual E1 potential is μ-integrable. There is B<∞ with ∫(−u)dμ≤B on normalized J(u)≤1. Otherwise choose u_j in that class with integrals ≥2^j. The actual convex restrictions w_m=Σ_(j=1)^m2^(−j)u_j, completed by the remaining reference weight, decrease, equal zero at vtriv and satisfy E(w_m)≥−1. Their nontrivial actual PSH limit w has finite energy, but ∫(−w)dμ=∞, a contradiction. For J(u)≥2^(−n), choose t=(2^nJ(u))^(−1/2); the segment bound gives ∫(−u)dμ≤B√(2^nJ(u)). For smaller J use B. Thus Lξ(μ)≤B+2^(n−2)B²<∞. This proves Lξ(μ)<∞ iff E1(ξ)⊂L1(μ), an intrinsic finite-energy TARGET criterion, not image sufficiency.

Accepted normalized roots are onto E1 and obey u/c≤Rξηu≤u/C≤0. Integrability of all source potentials therefore implies integrability of every target potential; the inverse gives the converse. Hence the finite-energy measure class is independent of Reeb field on the same K, without a strong-topology claim.

Actual fixed-ray concavity and first variation give E(w)≤E(u)+∫(w−u)dMA(u). Raw decreasing approximation and weighted continuity extend this to E1. For ν=MA(u), it yields Lξ(ν)=E(u)−∫u dν<∞, with equality obtained by using u as an E1 test. This proves necessity and genuine optimality. The opposite inequality printed at Wu2406.13684v1 LF1249 is not used.

For n2, the accepted outer functional is F(g)=sup_{w∈CPSH,w≤g}E(w), F↓(h)=inf_{g∈C(K),g≥h}F(g). It agrees with actual PSH energy and is decreasing-net continuous. One fixed dense lattice D has actual auxiliary representatives f=a−b, a/A,b/A∈CPSH(ξ). For |t|≤τ and actual E1 u, |F↓(u+tf)−E(u)−t∫f dMA(u)|≤C_f t², where C_f=2pA(1+Aτ)^(p−1)||f||; for p=0 the remainder is zero. These are precisely the accepted hypotheses used below.

notes.summary: Every finite-energy target has genuine FS approximate solutions with quantitative weak error, I-Cauchy potentials and bounded normalized energy. Any actual E1 limit solves the equation; actual completeness remains unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: Outer duality and both-sign differentiation give |(MA(u)−μ)(f)|≤d_u/s+C_fs. FS deficits below j^(−2) yield weak convergence of genuine probabilities. A reconstructed fixed-ray Hessian gives a_p I(u,v)≤E((u+v)/2)−(E(u)+E(v))/2, a_p=p/4^(p+1), hence I≤(d_u+d_v)/(2a_p). Auxiliary positive products give the MA continuity estimate √(2Ap||f||I). These results identify an actual limit but do not realize a formal completion. Dimension one is completely solved.
notes.text:
Use n1 for the actual cone classes, probability normalization, mixed products, Hodge index, finite dual energy, decreasing target integrability and accepted outer derivative. Fix ξ and μ on K with L=Lξ(μ)<∞. For genuine u∈E1 set d_u=L−E(u)+∫u dμ≥0.

For continuous g and feasible CPSH w≤g, positivity gives E(w)−∫g dμ≤E(w)−∫w dμ≤L. Therefore F(g)−∫g dμ≤L. If h is bounded-above usc and μ-integrable, take the decreasing net of continuous majorants below a fixed upper constant. Minima make it directed; compact Hausdorff normality and usc level sets give infimum h. The decreasing integral fact and outer continuity from n1 yield F↓(h)−∫h dμ≤L. Apply this to h=u+tf, which is integrable by n1.

The lower side of the accepted derivative estimate gives t∫f d(MA(u)−μ)≤d_u+C_f t² for f∈D. Taking t=s and t=−s proves |∫f d(MA(u)−μ)|≤d_u/s+C_f s, 0<s≤τ. If d_u=0, let s decrease to zero; density and mass one give MA(u)=μ. Conversely n1 gives d_u=0 for a solution. This is both-sign Euler–Lagrange on an already genuine potential, not an existence characterization by attainment.

Choose u_j∈H(ξ) with d_j<j^(−2), using the explicit FS supremum. Constants preserve deficits and MA. With τ=1 and s=1/j, |∫f d(MA(u_j)−μ)|≤(1+C_f)/j for f∈D. For arbitrary continuous f, approximate by f_m∈D and add at most 2||f−f_m|| because both measures are probabilities. Choose m before j. Thus the genuine MA measures converge weakly to μ on the fixed carrier, including irrational fields and nonmetrizable K. This uses a real supremum, not a countable enumeration of the ground field. The same argument covers any actual E1 maximizing net.

For p=n−1≥1, let z=u−v and define, initially for continuous actual same-field potentials,
B_j=−Vξ^(−1)∫z ddc z (ddc u)^j(ddc v)^(p−1−j)ddc ρξ^+≥0, 0≤j≤p−1.
Fixed-ray Hodge index gives nonnegativity. Integration by parts and the difference of powers give I(u,v)=∫(u−v)d(MA(v)−MA(u))=ΣB_j. For g(t)=E(v+tz), the actual product expansion gives −g''(t)=pΣ binom(p−1,j)t^j(1−t)^(p−1−j)B_j.

The midpoint Green kernel is G(1/2,t)=(1/2)min(t,1−t). Consequently H=E((u+v)/2)−(E(u)+E(v))/2=∫G(1/2,t)(−g''(t))dt≥a_p I(u,v), a_p=p/4^(p+1). On [1/4,3/4], the kernel is ≥1/8, each monomial ≥4^(−(p−1)), each binomial ≥1, and the interval length is 1/2. All B_j and I are expressible as sums of accepted weighted genuine mixed measures. Raw simultaneous decreasing CPSH approximation passes the inequality and coefficients to actual E1, without postulating new unbounded currents.

The actual midpoint deficit is (d_u+d_v)/2−H≥0. Therefore I(u,v)≤(d_u+d_v)/(2a_p), so every maximizing sequence is I-Cauchy modulo constants. Pair normalized u with the reference, whose deficit is L. The two nonnegative tangent deficits sum to I(u,ρ); the reference one is −E(u), since MA(ρ)=δ_vtriv and u(vtriv)=0. Hence −E(u)≤I(u,ρ)≤(d_u+L)/(2a_p). Normalized maximizing sequences have bounded finite energy. This is not compactness or actual completeness.

There is also a genuine continuity estimate. Represent f∈D by a−b with actual slope-A psh a,b and a/A,b/A∈CPSH(ξ). For M_j=(ddc u)^j(ddc v)^(p−1−j)ddc ρ^+, Hodge index and Cauchy–Schwarz give |V^(−1)∫f ddc z M_j|≤√(Q_j(f)B_j), where Q_j(f)=−V^(−1)∫f ddc f M_j≥0. Since ddc f=ddc a−ddc b, each positive product with a or b has normalized mass A: factor out A and use the genuine mixed probability for a/A or b/A. Thus Q_j(f)≤2A||f||. Sum the difference of powers and use Σ√B_j≤√(pΣB_j) to obtain |∫f d(MA(u)−MA(v))|≤√(2Ap||f||I(u,v)). Fixed-field decreasing approximation extends it to actual E1. Uniform density gives weak MA continuity whenever I(u_j,u)→0 with an actual E1 u.

An actual E1/R limit of the maximizing sequence would therefore give both MA(u_j)→MA(u) and MA(u_j)→μ weakly, forcing MA(u)=μ. Actual completeness on all normal cones is NOT proved. A formal completion cannot substitute for the missing potential. This measure-limit route avoids passing target integrals through a nonmonotone maximizing sequence; after a genuine solution exists, n1 gives its finite target integral and exact optimality. Arbitrary nonmonotone target-integration continuity is not asserted.

For n=1, the accepted effective normal grading gives R=k[z], K={vtriv}, potential restrictions are constants, E(u)=u(vtriv), and the empty horizontal product with the calibrated radial factor gives MA(u)=δ_vtriv. The sole probability is realized with dual energy zero, uniquely modulo constants. This does not solve the all-dimensional problem.

notes.summary: Carrier usc-envelope transport across Reeb fields is proved, but its rational singular base remains unverified. The public singular v1 lower-growth Proposition 4.19 has an explicit smooth-affine-line counterexample.
notes.detailedSummary: On the torified punctured cone Ω≅K×R, uniform orbit slopes prove R(sup u_i)=sup R u_i and R(U*)=(RU)*, including −∞ values. Thus carrier usc-sup stability transfers through raw roots without implying strong continuity or completeness. Independently, v=(log+|z|)^2 is locally psh by decreasing rational dyadic secants and satisfies the printed lower-growth condition, but cannot be a decreasing global FS limit. This disproves the proposition as printed, not a corrected final singular EP theorem. The corrected regularization, contact, trace, Runge, induction and descent chain remains unverified.
notes.text:
Use n1 for the accepted actual root maps, cone action, reference and class membership. Let Ω be the torified analytic points off the vertex. The accepted action (v+tη)(Σfα)=minα[v(fα)+t⟨η,α⟩] is jointly continuous; each fixed t is a homeomorphism with inverse −t. For homogeneous generators h_i of weights β_i, ρξ(v)=max_i[−v(h_i)/⟨ξ,β_i⟩] is finite continuous, and sξ(v)=v+ρξ(v)ξ∈K. The continuous inverse maps v↦(sξ(v),ρξ(v)) and (x,r)↦x−rξ give Ω≅K×R. Thus U(v)=h(sξ(v))+ρξ(v) has usc regularization U*(v)=h*(sξ(v))+ρξ(v), including extended values and arbitrary nets.

For a nonempty uniformly carrier-upper-bounded family of actual ξ-PSH potentials, put U=sup_i u_i. It is locally bounded above and satisfies U(v)−Ct≤U(v+tη)≤U(v)−ct, t≥0, with 0<c≤C controlling all supported degrees. U* satisfies the same inequalities by the fixed-action homeomorphisms. Each orbit is either identically −∞ or finite, Lipschitz, strictly decreasing and onto R. Define R U and R U* by their zero parameters, without claiming psh membership.

At v set r=sup_i R u_i(v). For t>r the uniform lower slope gives U(v+tη)≤−c(t−r)<0; for t<r some branch is positive. If r=−∞, all original orbits are −∞. Hence R U=sup_i R u_i. Also R U*=(R U)*: for t>R U*(v), upper semicontinuity gives a neighborhood of v+tη where U is strictly negative; pull back by the fixed inverse action to bound nearby roots below t. For t<R U*(v), every neighborhood of v+tη meets {U>0}; pull back to show every neighborhood of v meets {R U>t}. Arbitrary such t prove equality. If the root is −∞, the first argument applies to every real t. Local upper bounds exclude +∞.

Define carrier usc-sup stability at ξ by requiring (sup_i u_i|K)* to be the restriction of an actual ξ-PSH potential for every such family. Root images have uniformly bounded carrier suprema, since these are their values at vtriv and orbit slopes bound those values. If the property holds at η, apply it to the root family. The identities identify its envelope with R U*. The accepted raw inverse root is actual ξ-PSH and, by its zero set and ξ-equivariance, equals U* on Ω. Reversing fields proves equivalence. No openness of torification, full-link envelope equality or strong continuity is inferred.

An independently proved projective EP on the actual rational normal quotient would suffice for this carrier property, but order transport supplies no singular base. Arbitrary normal projective bases occur: for normal integral projective V and ample Cartier D, its full section ring is the intersection of k(V)[t] and the Gauss valuation rings assigning ft^m the value v_F(f)+m ord_F(D), over prime divisors F. Normality identifies sections by these codimension-one inequalities, so the intersection is integrally closed. Ampleness gives finite generation and a high standard Veronese with Proj V. Its scalar-torus normal cone is an original cone with quotient V and trivial residual torus. A universal smooth-quotient simplification therefore cannot cover the task.

The source diagnostic concerns E=Lyuhui Wu, arXiv:2609.27610v1. Its PDF SHA256 is 11808a6c9ede9c0158b27e16700fc180a4ac8df12a4586a7178e1958e8f6bba8; extract SHA256 c8ffe91a631da67f6d3872a1a06ab8d15755aed2f926cdf326725ca3662cef7d. Coordinates are inclusive one-based LF indices after UTF-8 byte decoding and split('\n'). Definition 3.15(2), LF766–768, requires an FS g with g≤v+O(1), a LOWER-growth condition. Regularizability at LF769–774 requires a decreasing global FS sequence. Proposition 4.19, LF1560–1562, asserts equality on smooth affine varieties. Its proof LF1569–1572 asserts the opposite upper bound and invokes Lemma 3.25(1), whose LF952–957 hypothesis already includes regularizability.

That lower-growth proposition is false as printed. On A1 over the original k let v=(max(log|z|,0))² and g=max(log|z|,0), both zero at z=0. The continuous finite v is locally psh in the exact Definition 3.8. On {|z|<e^M}, rational M>0, put t=−log|z| and use dyadic secant interpolation of t² on [−M,0], extended by zero for t≥0 including +∞. These rational PL interpolants are convex and continuous; on the finite coordinate part they are finite maxima of rational affine branches, and near +∞ they are constant zero. They meet the source’s local finite-valued affine and tropical-convex requirements. Nested dyadic refinement decreases them to (max(−t,0))². Composing with the z tropicalization supplies the required decreasing local TConv–PL sequences; the neighborhoods cover the affine analytification. The generator z with coefficient one and constant branch zero makes g an actual source-FS function. Since r≤r²+1/4 for r≥0, g≤v+1/4 everywhere, placing v in the printed lower-growth class.

On the Gauss seminorm of radius e^t, t≥0, every nonzero f∈k[z] has log|f|=(deg f)t because coefficients are trivially valued. Every source-FS function, a finite maximum of positive rational multiples of these logarithms plus rational constants and a constant branch, is bounded by At+B for finite A,B. A decreasing global FS sequence converging to v would have a first term majorizing v, forcing t²≤At+B for all t≥0, impossible. This independently proves the counterexample using the exact rational/local definitions.

Correcting the growth definition to an UPPER bound excludes this example, but does not prove corrected regularization/removal or validate the singular applications. The contact line LF1972 also prints comparison with l(t) rather than l(t'); changing that variable alone does not certify the construction. Complete pertinent trace, Rossi/Runge, singular-induction and descent bodies are retained, not imported. Theorem 6.3 LF1926–1929 and Theorem 6.5 LF1938–1941 have countable-dense-subfield hypotheses; Theorem 7.1 adds a descent argument needing independent checking. This note disproves the printed Proposition 4.19 formulation, NOT the final singular EP conclusion or a properly reconstructed corrected theorem.

notes.text:
The unchanged original P13.2 has not been solved. Notes n1–n3 establish, on every original normal cone and every Reeb field, an explicit FS finite-energy target criterion, quantitative genuine approximate solutions, I-Cauchy potentials with bounded normalized energy, actual-limit MA continuity and carrier usc-root envelope transport. Cone dimension one is realized exactly. None proves universal image sufficiency in higher dimensions.

The indispensable missing assertion for the Cauchy route is actual completeness or independent realization in E1(ξ)/R. A formal completion or closure through unknown outputs cannot replace it. An envelope route needs a verified singular normal rational base; root transport supplies no base. If using compactness variational limits, target integration continuity for the resulting nonmonotone limits must also be established. The decreasing-net continuity proved here is insufficient for that different route. The corrected public singular v1 regularization, contact, trace, Rossi/Runge, induction and arbitrary-field descent chain is not reconstructed. Its printed lower-growth Proposition 4.19 has the counterexample in n3, but its corrected final EP conclusion is not disproved.
